title: The Scientist and Engineer's Guide to Digital Signal Processing
where: The author/publisher's official site provides the complete book for free legal reading as browsable HTML and downloadable chapter PDFs at https://www.dspguide.com/pdfbook.htm. Its permissions page at https://www.dspguide.com/copyrite.htm explicitly permits downloading any or all of the electronic book for personal use.
toc: 1. The Breadth and Depth of DSP

shards.note: Foundations through applications of the DFT: breadth of DSP, statistics/noise, conversion, software, linear systems, convolution, and the real DFT. Read complete chapter HTML or the corresponding Chapter1.pdf through Chapter9.pdf files.
Fourier properties and pairs, FFT, continuous signals, and the first block of digital-filter design through FFT convolution. Read complete chapter HTML or Chapter10.pdf through Chapter18.pdf.
Recursive/Chebyshev filter design and comparison, followed by audio, imaging, and neural-network applications. Read complete chapter HTML or Chapter19.pdf through Chapter26.pdf.

Compression, DSP hardware and implementation, then complex numbers/transforms, Laplace and z transforms, and the Benford's-law case study. Read complete chapter HTML or Chapter27.pdf through Chapter34.pdf.

notes: The official contents page describes a 640-page book and exposes all 34 chapters, each as both navigable web text and a downloadable PDF. The official permissions page confirms that personal downloading of any or all of the electronic book is allowed. The site identifies Steven W. Smith as author and California Technical Publishing as copyright holder. Its editions page says the 1997 hardcover (ISBN 0-9660176-3-3) and the differently titled 2002 Newnes paperback are substantially the same book; chapters 28 and 29, omitted from the hardcover, remain part of the complete electronic edition. The four shards preserve chapter boundaries and distribute 34 chapters as 9/9/8/8.
